subject: Post-call: budget anchor + prefix-cache ops recap
messages:
From: Sophie Laurent <sophie@brightlayer.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-12T17:05:00-05:00
Subject: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget after today's demo

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the demo earlier — Sandy and I appreciated the throughput examples. Before we push to procurement I'd like to lock down a couple of items so I can give a clean ask to finance:

- Expected monthly token volume (best / likely / high).
- Target budget range we should use as an anchor (annualized).
- Any caching assumptions you used to generate the unit economics in the slides (hit rate, prefix vs full response caching).

Sandy mentioned you could share a simple model showing effective $/1M tokens under different hit rates. If you can send the model and a one-page summary we can include it in our business case.

Procurement timeline: aiming to decide by end of Nov — target PO early Dec.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Laurent
Head of Platform Partnerships, BrightLayer
(sophie@brightlayer.com)

Attachment: BrightLayer-demo-notes.pdf (referenced)

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Laurent <sophie@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-12T19:18:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget after today's demo

Hi Sophie — great to meet you and Sandy today. Short answers below and I've attached a working model (pricing-model-v2.xlsx) plus a concise summary (redwood-pricing-summary.pdf).

Quick anchors you asked for:
- Volumes (monthly):
  - Best: 50M input tokens / 100M output tokens (50M total approx)
  - Likely: 20M input / 40M output (20M total)
  - High: 120M input / 240M output (120M total)

  (We separate input/output for latency planning; for simple costing we use total tokens = input+output.)

- Budget anchor (annualized):
  - Low/POC: $15k–$35k / year (assumes heavy caching + small footprint)
  - Mid: $90k–$160k / year (likely scenario)
  - High: $540k+/year (large scale, low-cache)

Caching assumptions used in the sheet:
- Default prefix-cache approach: cache common leading prompts (API-level prefix caching). We assumed a 3-tier hit-rate scenario for effective cost: 25% / 50% / 70%.
- Prefix-cache effect is modeled as reducing output token generation for cache hits (we assume cached responses bypass ~75% of generation cost for that request).

Target unit economics (numbers in model are normalized to $/1M tokens before/after cache):
- Raw list price baseline: $2,500 per 1M tokens (example model placeholder).
- Effective $/1M at 25% hit: ~$1,900
- Effective $/1M at 50% hit: ~$1,350
- Effective $/1M at 70% hit: ~$850

Notes: those effective numbers include auto-batching and recommended 8-bit quantization profile in the model; we can change assumptions if your prompts are longer or you need higher quality.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Sophie — confirm which of the three monthly volume profiles is closest to your expectations (best/likely/high).
2) Ben — can you run a short prefix-cache sim (attached) with the BrightLayer prompt samples Sophie shared?
3) Sophie/Tim — if procurement wants an anchor, would you prefer we provide a firm committed monthly rate (Dedicated) vs a flexible hosted-rate example?

I'll stand by for the volume choice and Ben will push the sim.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
log an@redwood.ai

Attachments: pricing-model-v2.xlsx, redwood-pricing-summary.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Sophie Laurent <sophie@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-13T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget after today's demo

Adding the operational perspective and a quick simulation I ran (prefix-cache-sim.csv attached). Key takeaways from the sim using the sample prompts you shared: 

- Cache definition used: prefix cache keyed on the first 80 tokens (we treat identical leading 80 tokens as a hit). For templated prompts this captures most of the repetition.
- Hit-rate scenarios from sampled traffic:
  - Conservative: 18% hit (low template reuse across sessions)
  - Practical: 48% hit (moderate reuse + session affinity)
  - Optimistic: 68% hit (heavy reuse, many repetitive queries)

- Cost math (using the model baseline Logan shared):
  - Baseline list: $2,500 / 1M tokens (no cache)
  - Effective $/1M at 18% hit: $2,130
  - Effective $/1M at 48% hit: $1,420
  - Effective $/1M at 68% hit: $920

Rationale: prefix hits avoid ~78% of generation compute on average for the samples (smaller outputs still generated server-side for personalization but heavy decoding skipped). I included two columns in the CSV: per-request tokens avoided and resulting effective monthly tokens.

Operational notes for procurement:
- If BrightLayer wants a firm committed price (Dedicated), we can bake the expected hit rate into the commitment and give a blended $/1M.
- For hosted, we provide an example effective rate but final will vary with actual traffic — recommend a 90-day pilot to validate hit rates before a long-term commitment.

Happy to jump on a short call to explain the sim.

– Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: prefix-cache-sim.csv

From: Timothy Jones <tim.jones@fintechco.com>

Thanks Logan / Ben — this is very helpful. Sophie and I reviewed the anchors and the cost model. A few quick answers:

- Volume profile: "Likely" (we expect ~25–30M total tokens/month to start).
- Procurement preference: we'd like a short Dedicated commitment (6 months) if you can provide a blended effective $/1M based on the Practical hit-rate you ran (48%). That gives us predictability for our finance team.
- Timeline: we'll escalate to procurement this week; they asked for the sim CSV and the one-page summary for the package review (please confirm attachments are final).

Sophie — if you want, Logan and Ben can join the procurement call on Thursday at 2pm ET to walk through the model.

Timothy Jones
